title: Three-class land-cover map of the south-west edge of Buraydah from Sentinel-2, with an error matrix

headline.label: overall accuracy for three classes, from 180 blind reference points

service.name: Land Cover and Land Use Classification

data: Sentinel-2 Level-2A surface reflectance, tile 38RLQ, relative orbit 92.
method: Class definitions were written first, for a 30 × 30 m block: vegetation = at least 5 of 9 pixels reach NDVI 0.3 on one of three seasonal scenes (summer and autumn 2025, winter 2026), checked first.
Why three classes: in two earlier four-class attempts most errors sat on two undefined boundaries, thin plant cover (NDVI around 0.18) and loose sand versus exposed soil.
Training data relabelled under these rules: 38 rectangles and the 400 points from the earlier attempts, with 24 points reviewed again by eye.
Map: vegetation by the rule on the three classification scenes; built-up versus bare by a random forest of 300 trees on 34 spectral and texture features; then a 30 m majority filter.
limits: Most of the gain came from the class definitions (a numeric vegetation threshold and one class for sand and soil), not from a better classifier, so the map does not separate sand from exposed soil and fallow fields, and does not count plant cover thinner than NDVI 0.3. The vegetation reference is a numeric rule on independent scenes 5 to 20 days from the map scenes, so its accuracy measures how stable the rule is across dates more than interpretation. Built-up versus bare was judged by eye by the analyst on 10 m imagery, not in the field, and built-up is overstated (user's accuracy 73%).
